restatement: The card makes one mutable registry of filter definitions (name, params, description, paramNames, apply) the only place filters are listed, so render, spec() and analyze/validate all read it and a later card can add a row without touching dispatch. Filters take and return values, and the six built-ins coerce their input to text exactly as the output step does, so no existing template output changes. Filter calls are parsed once at parse time with quotes respected. A parameter a filter does not declare is a located type-error, not a silent fallback. An unterminated quote in a ?? default no longer swallows the filters after it. Two empty group files feed the registry. No runtime dependency is added and no template text is evaluated as code.
verification_plan: c1: confirm render, spec(), analyze and validate all read FILTER_REGISTRY at call time, with no load-time cache or second name list. Confirm spec() copies only name, params and description.
c2: confirm the six built-ins coerce input to text the way the output step does, and that arrays, objects, numbers and null reach a filter as values and print as they would unfiltered.

c3: trace parseFilter for fence="a=b", fence="a:b", the shorthand and named forms, and its old return shapes. Confirm an undeclared parameter becomes a type-error located at the variable in both strict and lenient mode.

c4: trace the ?? default split for a quote that never closes and for a closed quoted default that holds a pipe. Check that the retry terminates and that the default text is stripped the way the spec examples say.
c5: confirm filters-text.ts and filters-collection.ts export empty arrays that the registry spreads in after the six built-ins.
c6 and m1-m4: confirm the only existing test file touched is spec.test.ts, no built-in's output changed, no dependency was added and nothing is evaluated as code.

Goal-critical questions: can a filter be missing from render, spec or analyze? Does any existing template render differently? Does every bad filter call fail with a located error everywhere, including validate and analyze? Can a quote hide a pipe or truncate a value?
Polish: does spec() leak a field beyond name, params and description? Is there a second filter list?

findings.title: validate and analyze accept an undeclared filter parameter that render rejects

serves.scenario: escape_md:mode=block passes validate() and analyze() with no diagnostic, then render() fails with a type-error. The card goal and ADR 0003 want typos caught before a run by validate and analyze, and the brief asks whether every bad filter call fails with a located error.

findings.rubric: each criterion is met by the diff and its test (c3); goal-critical question 3: bad filter calls fail with a located error and never silently pass
findings.reproduction: Run validate('${{ v | escape_md:mode=block }}') and analyze on the same template, with no data. The diff's analyze.ts only checks FILTER_REGISTRY.some(f => f.name === name), so no diagnostic is produced and ok is true. render() on the same template returns a type-error at 1:1, because the paramNames check lives only in applyFilter. Each call is already parsed at parse time, so filter.params and the definition's paramNames are available in the analyze walker.
evidence: test:fr-args: an undeclared parameter is a type-error at the variable

findings.title: FILTERS is a load-time snapshot that goes stale when the registry changes

serves.scenario: FILTERS = listFilters() is evaluated once at module load, so a definition pushed into FILTER_REGISTRY later is missing from FILTERS. That is a second, stale copy of the filter list. The spec says no name is looked up once at load, and the brief says the registry is the only place a filter name is listed.

findings.rubric: the registry is the only place a filter name is listed (polish)
findings.reproduction: Push a definition into FILTER_REGISTRY after import and compare FILTERS.map(f => f.name) with FILTER_REGISTRY.map(f => f.name). They differ. Only a test taken at load time passes.
